newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MILAN'S BIGGEST DEFEAT WRITTEN IN SKIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MILAN'S BIGGEST DEFEAT WRITTEN IN SKIES.

text.p: On the eve of AC Milan's clash with Juventus on Sunday, their coach Arrigo Sacchi called on Comet Hale-Bopp to cast some light on his players.
The day after his side's historic 6-1 capitulation, the superstitious Sacchi could be forgiven for seeing the comet as a portent of footballing calamity as it cast nothing but darkness.

It was the first time they had conceded six goals in front of their own fans and was their worst home defeat in their 98-year history. It also equalled their biggest loss ever -- a 6-1 humiliation at Alessandria in the 1936-37 season.
And, even if Juventus's 7-1 defeat at home to Milan in 1951 remains the heaviest ever margin of defeat in this famous encounter, it offers scant consolation.
Juve went on to win the championship that year while this time around, Milan are seventh in serie A and struggling to qualify for next season's UEFA Cup.
The result, if not the comet, is the signal for another shift in the cyclical power which has seen the two clubs dominate Italian soccer over the past century.

"In another 100 years, people will still talk about this result, how Milan conceded six goals and surrendered their league title to their historic rivals," wrote sports daily Gazzetta dello Sport in a front page editorial.
